title: Power Cables
pages: Cables carry Forge Energy (FE) from any block that lets energy be extracted, such as this mod's Firebox Dynamo or another mod's generator or battery, into machines that accept it. Craft them on a crafting table: Tin Wire from three tin ingots (forge:ingots/tin) in a row, 6 wires. Copper Cable from three copper ingots between two rows of Carded Fiber, 6 cables. Silver Cable from silver ingots between Porcelain Insulators, 6. Aluminum Cable from aluminum ingots between Green Porcelain Insulators, 6. Niobium Line from five niobium ingots and four Green Porcelain Insulators, 4.

Each cable has a voltage class and current rating: Tin Wire 16 V x 2 A (32 FE/t, 400 mOhm per block), Copper 64 V x 4 A (256 FE/t, 160 mOhm), Silver 256 V x 4 A (1024 FE/t, 60 mOhm), Aluminum 1024 V x 8 A (8192 FE/t, 110 mOhm), Niobium 4096 V x 16 A (65536 FE/t, 5 mOhm). A run never moves more than its rating. Every delivery pays resistive I^2R loss that grows with the number of cable blocks crossed, so a long low-voltage run wastes power; a run long enough to drop its whole voltage (20 tin wires carrying the full 2 A) delivers nothing.

Condition: only cables of the same kind join; a copper cable beside a silver cable stays open, so each run keeps one voltage class. A generator that declares a class, such as the Trickle (16 V) Firebox Dynamo, only feeds a run of that class: touching a lower-class cable burns that cable (overvoltage, no drop), and a higher-class run takes nothing from it (undervoltage). Generators from other mods declare no class and feed any run. A cable face joins a neighbouring cable or any block with an energy port. Right-click a face with an empty hand to switch it off; the face stays off after saving and reloading the world, and switching it again re-links it. Cables store no energy, so breaking one loses nothing.

Automation: a cable touching an extractable energy holder pulls from it every 10 ticks (half a second) and feeds the receivers on its run nearest first, simulating each transfer before taking energy. Use switched-off faces as side configuration: turn off the face against a machine that should not be fed, or the face against a battery the run must not drain. Machines in this mod accept FE but never give it back, so a run from a generator through several machines fills the closest ones first.

Transformers join two neighbouring classes: Trickle-Low Transformer (16/64 V), Low-Medium Transformer (64/256 V), Medium-High Transformer (256/1024 V) and High-Surge Transformer (1024/4096 V). Craft each on a crafting table around a Laminated Transformer Core: the lower class's cable on the top and left, the higher class's cable on the right and bottom, and four ingots of the higher conductor's metal in the corners (copper, silver, aluminum, niobium). Mine with a pickaxe; it drops itself.

Use: the face pointing at you when placed is the high-voltage terminal (white or coloured insulator); the other five faces are the low-voltage terminal. Right-click with an empty hand to switch Step up (lamp chevron rising: low faces in, front out) or Step down (chevron falling: front in, low faces out). A transformer keeps no buffer: a run that reaches its input terminal at the input class carries on through it into the output run in the same push, at 96% efficiency, plus both runs' line loss. A run of the wrong class is refused, never converted.

Why step up: the same power at four times the voltage needs a quarter of the current and loses a sixteenth as much. Example: Firebox Dynamos on short Tin Wire into a Trickle-Low transformer, a long Copper Cable trunk, then a Low-Trickle step-down (another Trickle-Low transformer set to Step down) beside the machines. Automation: transformers are passive, so the trunk works whenever a generator runs; switch a cable face off to isolate a branch. At most four transformers can be chained in one push.

Machine voltage classes: every machine takes power only at the class of its tier, two tiers per class: Tier 0-1 Trickle (16 V), Tier 2-3 Low (64 V), Tier 4-5 Medium (256 V), Tier 6-7 High (1024 V), Tier 8-9 Surge (4096 V). A run of a lower class leaves the machine idle; a run of a higher class burns the cable touching the machine (no drop) and stops that push, so step the line down first. The Strata Excavator is Low, and the powered Arc Press and Induction Coiler frames are Medium: a Stock Hatch linked to their controller takes power at the controller's class, while an unlinked hatch takes nothing. The Firebox Dynamo feeds only Trickle machines it touches directly. Another mod's cables and generators skip this check. Datapacks can move a machine with the block tags arcana_industry:load_class/<class>.

Datapack ratings: data/arcana_industry/arcana_conductors/<cable>.json sets rated_current (1-64 A) and milliohms_per_block (0-10000) for tin_wire, copper_cable, silver_cable, aluminum_cable or niobium_line, and applies on /reload. The voltage class cannot change. Invalid or unknown files are ignored with a log warning and the values above stay.
